program: Free-clinic care, with blood-pressure treatment as the quantified pathway

nutshell.headline: Our best estimate is $3.40 million per 10 additional Bay Area QALYs.
nutshell.body: The overall US estimate is $2.89 million. This conditional model counts an entire unrestricted gift while quantifying its blood-pressure-care share; other clinic benefits remain unquantified. It is not a demonstrated below-$100,000 opportunity.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Sustained blood-pressure treatment can prevent cardiovascular events when patients would otherwise lack effective care.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Local risk, achieved treatment differences, marginal costs and donor additionality are not measured. The longer health consequences may overstate benefit if prevented events instead occur later.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Verify the complete care budget and sustained treatment difference beyond accessible alternatives. Actual Bay operations do not establish an SF-resident benefit share.

summary.label: Bay estimate
summary.detail: Central donor-cash estimate; $5.14M including gross associated resources.

summary.label: Overall estimate
summary.detail: All modeled US beneficiaries; includes Bay health, so the two are not additive.

summary.label: SF benefit
summary.detail: Zero SF health credited pending residence evidence—not a claim that no SF residents receive care.

programSection.body: RotaCare Bay Area, Inc. operates volunteer-supported clinics providing acute and chronic care. Northern Peninsula is in Daly City, not San Francisco; it lists prescriptions but no medication dispensing. Services and eligibility vary by clinic.

steps.title: Make sustained care accessible
steps.detail: Assessment, prescribing, testing and follow-up may help uninsured people obtain effective blood-pressure treatment.

steps.title: Improve outcomes beyond usual care
steps.detail: The model requires a sustained achieved blood-pressure difference—not merely screening, visits or referrals.

programSection.boundary: We assign 40% of a hypothetical $100,000 unrestricted gift to five-year blood-pressure care offers. The remaining 60% supports the broader clinic portfolio and remains in the cost numerator, with health unquantified. This allocation is an analyst prior, not a reported budget. Operation Access surgery benefits are excluded to avoid duplicate credit.

model.headline: A $100,000 gift yields an estimated 0.295 Bay QALYs.
model.body: The central model reserves $1,750 for each five-year offered care pathway, including unsuccessful participation, medicines, tests, coordination and allocated overhead. It funds 22.857 offers. Future cash is reserved at the gift date; no reserve interest or inflation is modeled.

equation.label: Central Bay model
equation.expression: 22.857 offers × .50 funding additionality × (.0313168 Q before shared harm − .001 Q shared harm) × .85 Bay share

inputs.label: Gift allocated to blood-pressure care
inputs.basis: All gift cash is counted once. Other clinic health is unquantified, not known to be zero.

inputs.label: Complete five-year cash cost
inputs.basis: Central annual budget: $60 medicines, $60 tests and $230 delivery/coordination/overhead. These are constructed budgets, not quotes.

inputs.label: Additional unpaid resources
inputs.basis: Donated clinical labor, facilities and other inputs outside cash; no duplicate medication or lab charge. Gross spending envelope, not net societal cost.

inputs.label: Usual-care five-year first-event risk
inputs.basis: No-new-gift cardiovascular risk; not a measured RotaCare cohort or universally untreated population.

inputs.label: Sustained systolic difference
inputs.basis: Average difference versus accessible care already incorporates receipt and persistence. No second adherence multiplier.

inputs.label: Major cardiovascular-event risk ratio
inputs.basis: Ettehad et al. randomized-trial meta-analysis. Exponentiation and transfer to local five-year risk are modeling assumptions.

inputs.label: Funding additionality
inputs.basis: Activity beyond existing grants, reserves, other donations and public care; distinct from clinical alternatives already embedded in the achieved BP difference.

inputs.label: Event-specific health consequences
inputs.basis: First events changed during five years of care are partitioned into fatal event, nonfatal stroke, MI and heart failure. Utility, survival and 3% discount are explicit assumptions; later event catch-up is not directly modeled.

inputs.label: Bay residence allocation
inputs.basis: Monterey and Santa Cruz are outside the nine-county Bay Area. These are residence priors, not clinic-count ratios; SF share is unverified.

model.giftHeading: How much could the estimate change?

sensitivity.headline: $122,413 / 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Joint optimistic assumptions; $195,861 with gross associated resources. Still above the target.

sensitivity.headline: $1.01 billion / 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Lower risk and treatment difference with more costly complete care; $1.39 billion gross.

sensitivity.headline: $15.92M / 10 Bay QALYs
sensitivity.detail: Only health flows through the end of care year 5 count; complete costs remain. Gross estimate: $24.11M.

sensitivity.headline: Not a demonstrated opportunity
sensitivity.detail: A sustained 30-mmHg difference gives $90,307 Bay cash but $144,491 gross. With health clipped at year 5: $491,691 cash and $786,706 gross. The local cohort and effect are unverified.

sensitivity.headline: No positive ratio
sensitivity.detail: Identical funding replacement or no clinical difference and no harm gives zero. Retained treatment harm can make health negative; independent gift harm may persist under replacement.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: These are analyst scenarios, not confidence intervals. First-event differences are scheduled over five years and discounted; mutually exclusive event consequences then receive finite survival/utility flows. Fatal events are not counted again as nonfatal injuries. The core assumes durable consequences of changed events; competing mortality alone does not resolve later cardiovascular catch-up. Clipping all flows at calendar year 5 is an explicit sensitivity, not an additional treatment duration.
model.fundingBoundary: The annual report’s $200 cost-per-patient figure is not a reconciled complete-cost price. FY2024–25 filing expenses of $1,413,811 divided by 1,582 reported unique patients are about $894—a scope cross-check, not a BP-course estimate. The model’s favorable $200 annual budget is a separate optimistic judgment. The report describes a CPA review, not an audit. Existing funds and donated resources remain baseline; full five-year staffing and follow-up capacity are not established. Gross associated resources are not net new societal costs when a gift replaces existing funding.

evidence.population: Blood-pressure treatment trials; Ettehad et al., 2016
evidence.result: A 10-mmHg systolic reduction was associated with a major cardiovascular-event risk ratio of .80.
evidence.transfer: Strong treatment anchor, not evidence that RotaCare achieves this incremental difference. Do not add separate mortality, stroke or heart-failure effects to the composite.

evidence.result: Higher-risk groups had larger absolute benefit from blood-pressure lowering.
evidence.transfer: Supports the importance of baseline risk; the local cohort risk remains unmeasured.

evidence.population: HOPE-3 intermediate-risk adults; separate 2024 coaching/practice-facilitation trial
evidence.result: HOPE-3 found no overall benefit in its intermediate-risk cohort; coaching/facilitation did not outperform enhanced usual care in the separate trial.
evidence.transfer: Care contact is insufficient by itself. Benefit depends on sustained additional treatment and risk.

evidence.population: Oxford Vascular Study stroke survivors and controls
evidence.result: Persistent utility loss after stroke supports a finite morbidity pathway.
evidence.transfer: Observational survivor-state evidence informs scale, not the causal utility of every cardiovascular event or a saved lifetime.

evidence.design: Provider program reports and tax filing
evidence.result: Actual chronic-care delivery and organizational finances are documented.
evidence.transfer: No measured next-gift allocation, achieved BP contrast or SF-resident share. Filing evidence does not establish a marginal care offer.

reservations: The central estimate and ordinary favorable scenario exceed $100,000 per 10 Bay QALYs.
The advertised $200 cost-per-patient figure is not a complete five-year care cost.
Clinical risk, treatment difference, funding additionality and Bay residence shares are analyst judgments.
Durable health consequences may be overstated if events are postponed rather than permanently avoided.
Actual Bay operations do not establish SF-resident health; no positive SF ratio is reported.
excludedBenefits: Unquantified acute, diabetes, asthma, diagnostic and other clinic benefits.
Operation Access partner surgery outcomes already represented elsewhere.
Additional cardiovascular events or separate all-cause mortality credit beyond the first-event model.
Unverified SF-resident benefits, healthcare savings and monetary opportunity-cost effects.
